wordings.text: What is the OET for veterinarians?
Which OET sub-tests are specific to veterinarians?

claims.text: Listening and Reading are not profession specific: they are common to all candidates.
The Writing task is specific to the candidate's own profession.
The Speaking role-play is specific to the candidate's own profession.

wordings.text: What OET score do veterinarians need?
What OET score do veterinarians need in the UK?
What OET score do veterinarians need in New Zealand?
Can veterinarians use OET@Home for Australia?

claims.text: The RCVS asks for an overall OET grade of B, with grade B or higher in three components and at least C+ in the fourth.
It accepts the veterinary version of the OET only, on paper or online.
The Australasian Veterinary Boards Council accepts English test results only from tests sat in person; online or at-home tests are not accepted.
The Veterinary Council of New Zealand asks for grade A or B in each of the four OET sub-tests, all from one sitting.

wordings.text: What OET score do veterinarians need in Ireland?

claims.text: The Veterinary Council of Ireland accepts an OET certificate with grade B or above, from an in-person exam only.
The certificate must be no older than two years on the date of submission.
The rule applies to applicants who obtained their qualification outside Ireland.

wordings.text: How much does the OET cost for veterinarians?
What is the OET fee for veterinarians in Pakistan in rupees?
Pakistan mein veterinarians ke liye OET ki fee kitni hai?

claims.text: OET lists the full four-part test at AU$587 (US$455 for the computer test at a venue or OET@Home in the USA).
Booking one, two or three sub-tests again on paper at a venue costs AU$315, AU$415 or AU$515, each including a AU$7 booking fee.

wordings.text: Where can I find OET practice tests for veterinarians?
Are there OET Writing and Speaking samples for veterinarians?

claims.text: OET publishes a Veterinary Science sample test for the computer test, with Listening, Reading and Writing questions, an answer key and a Speaking role card.

claims.text: The Writing sub-test takes 45 minutes and asks for a formal letter on a matter of the candidate's own profession, written from case notes.

wordings.text: How long do OET results take for veterinarians?

claims.text: Computer-test and OET@Home results can be made available within 48 hours of finishing all four sub-tests.
Paper-test results can be made available 12 days after the test date.

wordings.text: How long is an OET result valid for veterinarians?

claims.text: OET sets no validity period of its own: the bodies that recognise OET decide how long a result stays valid.

wordings.text: How do veterinarians book the OET?

claims.text: OET's booking page covers the paper test, the computer test at a test venue and OET@Home.
Bookings close 24 days before the test date for the paper test and 7 days before for the computer test and OET@Home.

wordings.text: Where can veterinarians take the OET in Pakistan?

claims.text: OET's website names Islamabad, Karachi and Lahore as the cities in Pakistan where computer-test candidates can take the Speaking sub-test at a venue.

wordings.text: What ID do veterinarians need on OET test day?

claims.text: On test day you can show your passport or national ID, and it must match the ID you booked with.

wordings.text: Can veterinarians move their OET test to another date?

claims.text: A computer-test or OET@Home booking can be moved up to two days before the first sub-test.
For the computer test and OET@Home, moving costs AU$120 before bookings close and AU$200 after.
